years.retained_earnings_note: Apple's retained earnings is negative (an accumulated deficit) in this year. This can be a normal result of returning capital to shareholders (dividends/buybacks) faster than cumulative net income -- common for mature, cash-generative companies -- not automatically a distress signal, though it does shrink the equity cushion the Z''-Score's X4 term relies on.
years.source: [USD] https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019323000106/aapl-20230930.htm | Consolidated Statements of Operations, Balance Sheets, Cash Flows, Apple Inc. FY2023 Form 10-K (shows FY2022 as prior-year comparative). Total Debt = Commercial paper + Term debt current + Term debt non-current (9,982+11,128+98,959). Receivables = Accounts receivable, net only (28,184); EXCLUDES Vendor non-trade receivables (32,748). Interest Expense = "Cash paid for interest" from supplemental cash flow disclosure (2,865) -- a REAL reported figure (cash basis), unlike FY2023/FY2024 where Apple stopped disclosing this line and only an estimate was available. Note this inconsistency: FY2022 interest expense is cash-paid, FY2023/24 are estimated from term debt x effective rate -- not perfectly comparable, flag in analysis.
